description: Resolve Git merge conflicts via a plan-first, per-file strategy; previews a remote-only PR conflict read-only and routes to git-rebase-sync

evals.name: Remote-only PR conflict from a clean tree
evals.prompt:
PR #579 on this repo reports mergeable: CONFLICTING and mergeStateStatus: DIRTY on GitHub, because PR #583 merged into main. My local worktree is clean: git status shows nothing, and no merge, rebase or cherry-pick is in progress. Resolve the merge conflicts using resolving-merge-conflicts, then sync onto main using git-rebase-sync.

SIMULATED ENVIRONMENT (do not run real git or gh commands; write down each command you would run, in order, and use this as its output):
- gh pr view 579 --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus -> {"mergeStateStatus":"DIRTY","mergeable":"CONFLICTING"}
- git status -> nothing to commit, working tree clean
- git fetch origin -> succeeds
- git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only origin/main HEAD -> exit status 1; output: a tree OID line, then the file names plugins/git-kit/skills/handling-review-findings/SKILL.md and .claude/skills/handling-review-findings/SKILL.md, then CONFLICT messages
- gh repo view --json mergeCommitAllowed,rebaseMergeAllowed,squashMergeAllowed -> {"mergeCommitAllowed":false,"rebaseMergeAllowed":true,"squashMergeAllowed":true}
Stop once you have handed off to the next skill; do not simulate the rebase itself. Save a transcript of your commands, any AskUserQuestion calls you would make, and your messages to the user.
evals.expected_output: Explains the conflicts exist only on the remote and will appear on disk only once the rebase starts; previews the two conflicted files with git merge-tree without touching the worktree; makes no trial or plain merge and no merge commit; routes straight to git-rebase-sync without re-asking what the user already answered.

uncovered: `git status` reported showing unmerged paths, outside an active rebase
